name: Broadcom
thesis: Broadcom is two businesses fused by Hock Tan's capital discipline: a custom-silicon + AI-networking franchise selling the 'anti-NVIDIA' pick-and-shovel to hyperscalers, and a high-margin infrastructure-software annuity (VMware) being repriced to subscription. The bet: hyperscalers who refuse to pay NVIDIA's gross margin co-design their own XPUs with the one vendor that has the SerDes/packaging/networking IP to build them — Google (7 TPU generations since 2014), Meta (locked through 2029), plus Anthropic and OpenAI. AI semi revenue hit $10.8B in Q2 FY26 (+143% YoY) and management guides ~$56B for FY26 with 'line of sight' to >$100B in 2027 against a $73B+ backlog. What the market under-models: networking is now ~40% of AI revenue — stickier, higher-margin, and far less contestable than the accelerator die itself; the franchise is a multi-customer, multi-generation TAM, not a single-socket bet. What's PRICED IN: at ~$1.84T and a ~24x forward P/E (64x trailing), the stock already discounts near-flawless execution toward that $100B number — there is little margin for error. The key risk is the mirror image of the bull case: AI revenue leans on ~3-6 customers, so any single hyperscaler program slip (Google or Meta) moves the whole growth line, on top of semi cyclicality, a $52B net-debt load still deleveraging post-VMware, and VMware price-hike churn. Right business, demanding price.
key_driver: AI semiconductor revenue growth (custom XPUs + AI networking) sustaining toward the $100B-in-2027 trajectory, with consolidated margin and post-VMware deleveraging intact — concentration in ~3-6 hyperscaler customers is the offsetting fragility.

nuance.bear_case: AI revenue is concentrated in roughly three-to-six hyperscaler customers (Google, Meta, plus Anthropic/OpenAI), so a single custom-XPU program slip, in-sourcing decision, or design-win loss at Google or Meta moves the entire AI growth line — there is no diversification cushion at the magnitude that matters. Layered on top: semiconductors remain cyclical and the AI capex cycle can roll over hard; the stock at ~$1.84T / ~24x forward already discounts the $100B-2027 outcome, so even a deceleration (not a decline) compresses the multiple violently; VMware's aggressive price hikes and bundle-only licensing are driving customer churn and goodwill damage that could cap the software annuity; and $52B of net debt, while deleveraging, limits flexibility if the cycle turns.
nuance.adversarial_take: 143% AI growth and a $73B backlog are spectacular, but 'line of sight to $100B in 2027' is a management aspiration the market has fully capitalized — buying here is paying a flawless-execution price for a business whose growth depends on a handful of customers' capex budgets. Backlog is bookings, not recognized revenue; hyperscaler in-sourcing (Google's own TPU competence, Meta's MTIA) is exactly the capability AVGO sells, so the long-run question is whether the customer becomes the competitor. The right posture is to want the business at a price that respects the concentration tail, not the current one.
nuance.stress_test: If AI semiconductor revenue growth drops below 40% YoY for two consecutive quarters AND a major customer (Google or Meta) publicly reduces or in-sources a custom-silicon program, the concentration thesis breaks: the backlog becomes a forward-guidance liability rather than a coiled spring, and a ~24x-forward multiple on decelerating, customer-dependent growth re-rates toward a cyclical semi multiple.

competitive_watchlist: NVIDIA (merchant GPU — the margin AVGO's custom-ASIC pitch undercuts)
Hyperscaler in-sourcing (Google TPU team, Meta MTIA, Amazon Trainium/Annapurna)
Nutanix / Red Hat / Microsoft (VMware virtualization-stack churn destinations)
thesis_breakers_qualitative: AI semiconductor revenue declines YoY in any quarter, or grows <40% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs (the AI ramp is the thesis)
A top custom-silicon customer (Google or Meta) reduces, in-sources, or loses a multi-generation XPU program — concentration risk realized
Consolidated gross margin falls below ~58% for 2 consecutive Qs (custom-ASIC volume diluting blended margin without software offset)
Net debt rises YoY for 2 consecutive Qs while FCF is flat/down — deleveraging stalls or AVGO re-levers for a large dilutive acquisition
VMware churn accelerates such that infrastructure-software revenue declines YoY — the annuity offset to semi cyclicality erodes

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters — outright top-line contraction.
GAAP operating margin negative for 2 consecutive quarters — operating loss.
Gross margin below 20% for 2 consecutive quarters — severe pricing/cost issue.

business_model_rules.narrative: AI semiconductor revenue growing <40% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — the custom-XPU + networking ramp (ran +106% Q1, +143% Q2 FY26) is decelerating toward exhaustion; this is the central thesis line. (UNRESOLVED until AI-semi revenue is backfilled as a KPI series.)
Total revenue growth below 10% YoY for 2 consecutive Qs — AI ramp exhausted with no software offset (FY26 ran +29% to +48%+ per quarter).
GAAP operating margin below 35% for 2 consecutive Qs — mix shift to lower-margin ASIC volume or a software stall (ran ~45% Q1 FY26).
Consolidated gross margin below 58% for 2 consecutive Qs — custom-ASIC volume diluting the blended margin faster than high-margin software lifts it (ran ~65-66% in FY26).
FCF margin below 25% for 2 consecutive Qs — cash conversion eroding despite growth, threatening dividend + deleveraging capacity (Q1 FY26 FCF was 41% of revenue).
